description: Also known as the Swamp Deer, famous for the adult male's magnificent multi-tined antlers; Madhya Pradesh's state animal.
habitat: Swampy grasslands, marshlands, and moist deciduous forest glades

description: Maharashtra's state animal (Shekru), a strikingly colorful tree squirrel leaping between canopy branches of moist forests.
habitat: Tropical moist deciduous and evergreen forest canopy

description: A large, tufted nocturnal raptor inhabiting rocky cliffs, ravines, and dry hill scrub, known for its deep resonant call.
habitat: Rocky outcrops, river ravines, dry scrub forest, old ruins

description: India's national bird, famed worldwide for the male's iridescent blue crest and train of eye-spotted feathers.
habitat: Open dry forest, thorn scrub, agricultural mosaic, riverbanks

habitat: Tropical evergreen island forest

description: A dark-coated, island-endemic macaque subspecies living along the coastal rainforests of Great and Little Nicobar.
habitat: Coastal mangroves and tropical evergreen island forest

habitat: Alpine meadows, high mountain scree slopes, steep rocky cliffs above tree line

habitat: Tropical rainforest, deciduous woodland, dry scrubland, mountain slopes

habitat: Tropical evergreen, moist deciduous forest, dry scrub

habitat: Arid and semi-arid scrub, rocky ravines, dry deciduous woodlands

habitat: Arid plains, open scrubland, agricultural farmland, dry deciduous woodland

habitat: Arid desert sand dunes, dry scrub, open plains, stony hills

habitat: Saline desert mudflats, arid salt marshes, scrub islands (bets)

habitat: Subalpine oak-rhododendron forests and high alpine meadows

habitat: Natural freshwater marshes, flooded agricultural fields, shallow wetlands

habitat: Shallow saline lagoons, mudflats, salt pans, coastal estuaries

habitat: Dry deciduous teak forests of Central India

habitat: Freshwater marshes, lakes, flooded fields, riverbanks

habitat: High-altitude mountain lakes (summer), freshwater reservoirs and rivers (winter)

habitat: Open cultivated fields, dry forest edges, roadside trees

habitat: Urban cities, towns, villages, coastal settlements

description: Affectionately called the 'Whistling Schoolboy' due to its musical human-like whistling song heard at dawn along Western Ghats streams.
habitat: Rocky forest streams, damp ravines, dark understory of Western Ghats

description: A colorful floor-dwelling jewel bird featuring nine distinct colors on its body, migrating seasonally between North and South India.
habitat: Moist deciduous forest floor, dense scrub undergrowth, shaded gardens

habitat: Woodlands, agricultural fields, urban parks, and dry tropical countryside.

Andhra Pradesh State Wildlife Symbols Notification (2018)

habitat: Wetlands, agricultural fields, mangrove channels, and forest ponds.
sourceCitations: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

description: Frugivorous pigeon with vibrant green plumage, lilac shoulder patches, and bright yellow feet, designated as the official State Bird of Maharashtra.
habitat: Tropical rainforests, banyan groves, and moist deciduous woodlands.
sourceCitations: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

description: Stocky ground pigeon with brilliant metallic emerald-green wings and soft pinkish-grey underparts, designated as the official State Bird of Tamil Nadu.
habitat: Dense tropical rainforests, Western Ghats thickets, and bamboo reserves.
sourceCitations: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

description: Glossy black bird with bright yellow head wattles, renowned for its incredible vocal mimicry, designated as the official State Bird of Meghalaya and Chhattisgarh.
habitat: Subtropical evergreen hill forests and moist forest canopies.
sourceCitations: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

description: Cuckoo species famed in Indian poetry for its resonant whistle, designated as the official State Bird of Jharkhand and Puducherry.
habitat: Open tropical woodlands, orchards, and suburban gardens.
sourceCitations: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

description: Medium-sized wild cat specially adapted to wetland environments with webbed paws for hunting fish, designated as the official State Animal of West Bengal.
habitat: Sundarbans mangroves, freshwater marshes, and riverine swamps.
sourceCitations: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

description: Substantial bovine species of Northeast India with distinct white stockings, designated as the official State Animal of Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland.
habitat: Subtropical montane forests, hill tracts, and bamboo clearings.
sourceCitations: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

description: Gentle marine herbivore that grazes on underwater seagrass meadows, designated as the official State Animal of Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
habitat: Shallow coastal marine waters, sheltered bays, and seagrass beds.
sourceCitations: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

description: One of the most familiar birds in Indian towns and cities, recognized by its chocolate-brown body, glossy black hood, and the bare yellow skin patch behind each eye. This highly adaptable omnivore forages on lawns and pavements in pairs, defends its nesting territory aggressively against rivals, and gathers in communal roosts that can number in the thousands at dusk.
habitat: Urban areas, farmland, and open scrub close to human settlement

description: A common garden and scrubland bird easily told apart by its short, squarish crest, scaly dark-brown body, white rump, and the splash of red under its tail. It feeds on fruit, nectar, and insects in dry scrub, open forest, and cultivated land, and builds a cup nest low in bushes during the June-to-September breeding season across most of the subcontinent.
habitat: Dry scrub, open forest, plains, and cultivated land

description: Ancestor of the domestic and feral pigeons seen in almost every Indian city, the rock pigeon has pale grey plumage with two dark wing bars and an iridescent green-and-purple sheen on the neck. Naturally a cliff-nesting species, it now breeds on building ledges nationwide, forages on the ground in large gregarious flocks, and is monogamous, typically raising two chicks per brood.
habitat: Cliffs and rocky terrain naturally; building ledges and urban open ground today

description: An all-black bird with a sharply forked tail, well known for perching conspicuously on wires and bare branches while sallying out after insects. Despite its small size it is fiercely territorial, mobbing and chasing off much larger crows and birds of prey that stray near its nest, a trait that has made it a familiar sight over farmland and open country nationwide.
habitat: Open agricultural land and light forest edges

description: A big, all-black crow with a heavy, arched bill and a glossy purple sheen to its plumage, often confused with the smaller house crow. It is an opportunistic omnivore that forages on the ground and in trees across woodland, parkland, and cultivated country, and is bold enough to scavenge readily around towns and villages wherever it occurs.
habitat: Woodland, parks, gardens, and cultivated land with trees

description: A tiny, bright-green warbler with creamy underparts, a rufous cap, and a long tail typically cocked upright. Named for its habit of stitching leaves together with plant fibre to build a concealed nest pouch, it stays mostly hidden in scrub and garden foliage but gives away its presence with a loud, repeated 'cheeup-cheeup-cheeup' call heard across gardens and farmland throughout the subcontinent.
habitat: Open farmland, scrub, forest edges, and urban gardens

description: A stocky, well-camouflaged heron, streaked olive-brown while standing still but revealing bright white wings the instant it takes flight. Also called the paddybird, it stalks fish, crustaceans, aquatic insects, and tadpoles at the edge of ponds and paddy fields, standing motionless for long stretches, and its dull plumage lets observers approach unusually close before it moves.
habitat: Marshes, ponds, paddy fields, and other shallow wetlands

description: A medium-sized bird of prey identified in flight by its angled wings and shallow forked tail, commonly seen gliding on thermals over towns and rubbish dumps. Largely a scavenger and opportunistic hunter, the Indian subspecies reaches some of the highest urban raptor densities recorded anywhere in the world, thriving in cities while generally avoiding heavily forested country.
habitat: Urban areas, open country, and farmland, avoiding dense forest

description: A slim, long-tailed dove with warm buff-brown plumage and a distinctive black collar finely spotted with white on the back and sides of the neck. It forages on the ground for seeds and grain, usually in pairs or small groups, and favours lightly wooded country, gardens, and urban parks, tending to occur in moister regions than the closely related laughing dove.
habitat: Light forest, gardens, cultivated land, and urban parks

description: Also known as the crow pheasant, this large, non-parasitic cuckoo has a glossy black head and body, chestnut wings, and striking ruby-red eyes. A weak flier, it moves mostly by clambering through undergrowth or walking on the ground, hunting insects, snails, small vertebrates, and the eggs and chicks of other birds across jungle edges, farmland, and even city gardens.
habitat: Jungle edges, scrub, cultivated land, and urban gardens

description: A large, sharply marked wader with a black head and bib, brown back, and a bright red fleshy wattle in front of each eye. Usually seen in pairs or small groups near water, it is famous for its loud, scolding 'did-he-do-it' alarm call, given persistently at any intruder near its nest, and it occurs at almost any wetland habitat across South Asia.
habitat: Open wetlands, grassland, and farmland near water

description: A small, confident songbird with a long, often cocked tail; males are glossy black and white with a bold white shoulder patch, while females wear a softer grey-and-white version of the same pattern. It favours open woodland and gardens close to people, foraging on the ground for insects, and males sing loudly and persistently from treetop perches through the breeding season.
habitat: Open woodland, gardens, and cultivated land near settlements

description: A lively, crested bulbul with brown upperparts, whitish underparts, and a small crimson streak below the eye that gives the species its name. Its tall, pointed black crest and loud, cheerful call make it conspicuous in lightly wooded country, scrub, and farmland, where it often announces itself from a treetop perch, especially in the early morning.
habitat: Lightly wooded country, scrub, and farmland

photoAttribution.author: Charles Lam from Hong Kong, China

description: A slender, brilliantly coloured bee-eater, almost entirely grass-green with a blue-tinged chin and throat, rufous crown, and two long central tail feathers. It hunts flying insects from low, open perches with quick sallying flights and is highly social, gathering to roost communally in groups of up to a few hundred birds in grassland and open scrub country.
habitat: Grassland, open scrub, and cultivated land

description: A tiny nectar-feeder under 10 centimetres long, with a fine down-curved bill built for probing flowers. Breeding males show iridescent purplish-black plumage that flashes metallic in sunlight, while females are olive-brown above with pale yellow underparts. It feeds mainly on nectar and small insects in gardens and thin forest, usually perching to feed rather than hovering like a hummingbird.
habitat: Thin forest, scrub, and garden land, including dense urban areas

description: A small waterbird that turns glossy all-black with a short crest and white facial flecks in the breeding season, appearing plainer brown with a whitish throat at other times. It dives from the surface to chase small fish in ponds, lakes, and streams, and frequently perches with wings spread wide to dry after fishing, a habit shared with other cormorants.
habitat: Ponds, lakes, streams, and other shallow freshwater bodies

description: A diminutive nectar-feeder under 10 centimetres long, with a thin down-curved bill and brush-tipped tongue built for sipping flowers. Males show dark maroon upperparts, a blue-green crown, and a violet rump patch, while females are plainer olive-brown with yellowish underparts. A common resident of gardens, scrub, and cultivated land across peninsular and eastern India, it stays away from dense, unbroken forest.
habitat: Gardens, scrub, and cultivated land with scattered trees

description: A small, active warbler with short rounded wings and a long, graduated tail tipped in cream and black. It flits through scrubland, grassland, and garden hedges hunting insects, and during its bouncing display flight produces a distinctive crackling, spark-like sound. Widespread across most of India, it thins out toward the drier northwest and the Himalayan foothills mark the edge of its range.
habitat: Dry open grassland, scrubland, and garden hedges

description: A striking, long-tailed corvid with a black head, cinnamon body, and a bluish-grey tail tipped in black. Conspicuous and noisy, it moves through open forest, scrubland, and gardens in small groups, giving a wide repertoire of calls including a distinctive bob-o-link. Populations across the subcontinent vary subtly in size and brightness, and Himalayan birds shift elevation seasonally.
habitat: Open forest, scrubland, and gardens

description: A stocky green barbet with a brown, white-streaked head and a bold white cheek stripe, endemic to the hill forests of southern India. Mostly a fruit-eater, it excavates its own nest cavities in tree trunks and stays still and well-camouflaged in the canopy, making it far easier to hear than to see.
habitat: Western Ghats forest and adjoining hill forest of southern India

description: A slender all-white heron with a fine black bill, black legs, and yellow feet, common at wetlands, rivers, and coastlines across India. It hunts small fish and aquatic invertebrates with an active style, often running through shallow water with wings raised or stirring the bottom with a shuffling foot to flush prey.
habitat: Wetlands, rivers, coastlines, and paddy fields

description: A drab, brownish-grey babbler with a yellow bill, best known for moving in noisy, sociable flocks of six to ten birds that gave rise to its popular local nickname, the "seven sisters." Found across forests and cultivated land through much of the subcontinent, with a paler subspecies adapted to the deserts of Rajasthan and the Rann of Kutch.
habitat: Forest edges, scrubland, and cultivated land

description: A small, confident bird of open scrub, males mostly black with a white shoulder patch and females plain brownish-grey. It runs along bare ground and low walls with its tail cocked upright, hunting insects, and different populations across the subcontinent vary between brown-backed and all-black-backed males.
habitat: Open scrub, bare ground, and rocky country

photoAttribution.author: PJeganathan, cropped & flipped left-right for taxobox use by MPF

description: A small green barbet with a crimson forehead and breast patch and yellow cheeks and throat, named for its metronomic "tuk...tuk...tuk" call that resembles a coppersmith's hammer. Almost entirely fruit-eating, it frequents gardens, groves, and open woodland, and is scarcer in India's arid northwest than across the rest of the subcontinent.
habitat: Gardens, groves, and sparse woodland

description: A medium-sized raptor with a white head and breast set against chestnut body plumage and black wingtips, common along coasts, rivers, and inland wetlands. Largely a scavenger of dead fish and crabs, it also takes live prey opportunistically, and in the Himalayan foothills it has been recorded soaring above 5,000 feet.
habitat: Coastal areas, rivers, and inland wetlands

description: A small, pinkish-brown dove with a chequered patch of black-and-white speckling on its neck, common in dry scrub, semi-desert, and cultivated land. It forages on the ground for fallen seeds and small insects, and pairs perform head-bobbing courtship displays accompanied by a soft, bubbling coo.
habitat: Dry scrub, semi-desert, and cultivated land

description: A dark slaty waterbird with a clean white face, breast, and belly, bolder and more visible than most rails as it walks across open marsh vegetation with its short tail flicked upright. Active mainly at dawn and dusk, it gives loud croaking calls through the breeding season and occurs from the plains up to over 1,000 metres in the hills.
habitat: Marshes, ponds, and vegetation at the water's edge

description: A golden-backed woodpecker with a black rump and a finely white-marked black throat that distinguishes it from other goldenbacks, well adapted to wooded avenues in towns as well as natural forest. Found widely across the subcontinent up to about 1,200 metres elevation, it thins out toward the arid Kutch and Rajasthan desert country.
habitat: Open forest, wooded farmland, and tree-lined urban avenues

description: A pale grey-buff dove with a neat black half-collar edged in white at the nape, easily told by its flat, three-syllable "goo-GOO-goo" call. It breeds readily close to people wherever grain and food scraps are reliable, and its historic range across warm temperate and subtropical Asia runs from Turkey through India to Sri Lanka.
habitat: Farmland, villages, and urban areas near a reliable food supply

description: A ground-dwelling gamebird with finely barred grey-brown plumage and a pale face bordered by a thin black throat line, common across open cultivated land and scrub forest. A weak flier, it prefers to escape danger by running into cover, and it is found through most of the subcontinent south of the Himalayan foothills, rarely above 500 metres.
habitat: Open cultivated land and scrub forest

description: A swift, agile bird with steel-blue upperparts, a rufous throat, and a deeply forked tail, seen hawking insects low over farmland, pasture, and open water. India hosts large numbers of migratory barn swallows through the winter months, in addition to a breeding population recorded in Sikkim.
habitat: Open farmland and pasture, usually near water

description: A small, active bird of scrub and forest edge; breeding males show a black cap and back against green wings, while females are a soft olive throughout. Males perform an elaborate courtship display, fluffing their feathers and spiralling down from a perch, and populations across India vary in exactly how much black the male shows on the head and mantle.
habitat: Scrub, forest edge, and wooded gardens

photoAttribution.author: Flickr user NatureAtYourBackyard . Photo uploaded to commons by user ltshears

description: One of the smallest birds in the region at around 8 centimetres, plain olive-brown with a slim, pale, downcurved bill. It feeds on nectar and berries in forest and garden alike, and by passing mistletoe seeds through its gut largely undamaged, it plays an outsized role in spreading this parasitic plant through the treetops of southern India.
habitat: Forest and garden trees across southern India

description: A small, upright perching bird; males are boldly black with white patches on the rump, wing, and lower belly, while females are a drab, streaked brown. It hunts insects from low perches in open country, and its regional populations shift seasonally, arriving on the Karwar coast each October and leaving by May, while remaining absent from Gujarat outside the winter months.
habitat: Open grassland and scrub, often near cultivation

description: A slim, pale brown swift with long, swept-back, crescent-shaped wings and a deeply forked tail, spending almost its entire life on the wing. It feeds and even drinks in flight, and its strong association with palm trees — where it glues its tiny nest to the underside of a frond — makes it a familiar sight over open country and cultivation across tropical India.
habitat: Open country and cultivation with palm trees

description: A tall, grey-and-white wading bird standing up to a metre high, found at lakes, rivers, marshes, and coastlines. It hunts by standing motionless or wading slowly through shallow water before striking at fish with a swift thrust of its long bill, and its range extends from Europe through the Middle East into India.
habitat: Lakes, rivers, marshes, and coastlines

description: A tiny, sociable bird with yellowish-olive upperparts, a bright white ring around the eye, and a yellow throat, usually seen foraging in small, active flocks for nectar and insects. Widespread across the subcontinent, hill populations in the Western Ghats and southern hills are recognized as distinct from the birds of the northern plains.
habitat: Gardens, forest edge, and scrub
